items.title: Home
items.text:
pq-glue copies the row groups of several Parquet files into one new file. Each column chunk is copied as bytes: it is not decompressed, decoded or re-encoded. The time it takes depends on the number of bytes copied, not on the number of columns or how deeply they are nested.

>>> import pq_glue
>>> pq_glue.concat(["part-0.parquet", "part-1.parquet"], "claims.parquet")
3
>>> import pyarrow.parquet as pq
>>> pq.read_table("claims.parquet").column("id").to_pylist()
['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3']
>>> pq.ParquetFile("claims.parquet").metadata.num_row_groups
2
  • concat returns the number of rows written.
  • The output has each input's row groups, in input order: here one from each file.
  • The inputs must have one Parquet schema. Files that differ are refused, and nothing is written.

items.title: pq-glue
items.text: Concatenate Parquet files without decoding them.

items.title: Where to go

  • What is copied: every part of the output file, and where it comes from.
  • Column orders: why the copied float statistics need a change to the footer, and how pq-glue makes it.
  • Benchmarks: pq-glue against Polars and pyarrow, on generated files and on Wikidata claims.

items.title: Install
items.text:
pip install pq-glue

cargo add pq-glue

The Python package needs Python 3.10 or later and has no Python dependencies.

items.title: Contents of the output file
items.text: part of the file in the output column chunks copied as bytes: the same pages, encodings and compression statistics each row group's min, max and null counts, readable by pyarrow page indexes, bloom filters copied where the inputs have them schema the first input's Parquet schema and ARROW:schema column orders the inputs', so float statistics stay valid

items.title: Performance
items.text: On the claims of 66 Wikidata chunks (555 MB, 9.4 million rows, 93 nested leaf columns), concat took 1.1 to 1.5 s and 0.6 s of CPU. Polars took 61 s (238 s of CPU) and pyarrow 56 s. The benchmarks page has the full figures and how to reproduce them.

items.title: Benchmarks
items.text:
pq-glue against the two usual ways of concatenating Parquet files from Python:

method code Polars pl.scan_parquet(src).sink_parquet(dst) pyarrow each row group read with ParquetFile.read_row_group and written with ParquetWriter.write_table (zstd) pq-glue pq_glue.concat(src, dst)

All figures are from a 4-core Intel Xeon at 2.1 GHz with Python 3.13. Ranges are the lowest and highest of 3 rounds.

items.title: Generated files
items.text:
24 files from bench/make_data.py: 131 MB, 1.44 million rows, one row group per file.

method wall (s) CPU (s) peak RSS (MB) Polars 4.79–5.29 17.41–18.72 735–786 pyarrow 7.27–7.35 8.25–8.38 291–307 pq-glue 0.23–0.28 0.23–0.27 11–12

pq-glue took about 1/20 of Polars' wall time and 1/70 of its CPU time. Its peak memory is that of the copy buffer and the footers: it does not grow with the number of rows.

items.title: Wikidata claims
items.text:
The claims partition files of 66 Wikidata chunks, from wikidata-pq: 555 MB, 9,372,174 rows in 114 row groups, 93 leaf columns nested up to lists of structs of lists. Measured in-process:

method wall (s) CPU (s) peak RSS Polars 61 238 2.2 GB pyarrow 56 74 0.8 GB pq-glue 1.1–1.5 0.6 87 MB (the whole Python process)

Decoding and re-encoding cost more for deeply nested columns, where every value has repetition and definition levels to rebuild. pq-glue does neither, so its time depends only on the bytes copied. It was about 20 times faster than Polars on the flat generated files, and about 50 times faster on the claims.

items.title: In a pipeline
items.text:
wikidata-pq processes Wikidata in chunks and merges each group of chunks' partition files before uploading them. On 66 chunks with 6 workers and groups of 22 chunks, merging the claims with pq-glue instead of Polars changed the whole run as follows (3 runs each, interleaved):

Polars pq-glue wall 182.9–185.6 s 131.7–134.8 s CPU of the merges 270–275 s 46–48 s peak RSS 10.0–10.3 GB 9.3–10.5 GB

The remaining merge CPU is the other tables, which wikidata-pq still merges with Polars. Both runs' outputs have the same rows in the same order, with the same schema, for every table and partition key.

items.title: Checking the outputs
items.text: In each benchmark, the first round's outputs must agree before any times are recorded: the same row count, and the same two sums of position-seeded row hashes, read with Polars. Any difference stops the run.

items.title: How it is timed
items.text:
• Processes: each method runs in a fresh Python process, in a different order each round.
  • Times: wall and CPU time (user and system) cover the concatenation only, not the imports.
  • Memory: peak RSS is the process's VmHWM, so the figures are for Linux only.

items.title: Reproducing
items.text:
The scripts are in bench/, a uv project that installs pq-glue from the repository:

cd bench
uv run make_data.py          # 24 files of 60,000 rows each in data/, about 131 MB
uv run run.py --rounds 3     # times each method and checks their outputs agree

To run the same comparison on your own files:

uv run run.py --files 'path/to/*.parquet'

Each run is appended to bench/results.jsonl.

items.title: Concepts
items.text:
A Parquet file is a sequence of row groups followed by a footer. Each row group has one column chunk per leaf column. The footer records the schema and, for every column chunk, where it starts, how long it is, its encodings, its compression and its statistics.

To concatenate files, pq-glue:

  1. reads each input's footer (and page indexes, if any);
  2. checks that the inputs share one schema, key-value metadata and column orders;
  3. copies each input's column chunks, in order, to the output as bytes;
  4. writes a new footer, with each column chunk's offsets moved to its new position;
  5. restores the inputs' column orders in that footer (Column orders).

No page is decompressed or decoded, so the cost is that of copying the bytes, and the memory used does not grow with the size of the files.

  • What is copied
  • Column orders

items.title: Column orders
items.text: The footer of a Parquet file declares, for each leaf column, the sort order its min/max statistics use. For most types this is the type-defined order. For floats, the Parquet format also defines IEEE 754 total order, which orders NaN and signed zeros and requires each column chunk's statistics to carry a NaN count.

items.title: The problem with a plain copy
items.text: parquet-rs (v60) declares IEEE 754 total order for every float column of a file it writes, whatever order the statistics in it were computed in. pyarrow writes float statistics in the type-defined order, without NaN counts. After a plain copy of pyarrow files, the output declares IEEE 754 total order for statistics that do not follow it, and Arrow C++ (so pyarrow) ignores their min and max.

items.title: What pq-glue does
items.text:
After parquet-rs writes the output's footer, pq-glue rewrites its column_orders list to the inputs' orders. In Thrift's compact encoding each entry is 3 bytes either way (1C 00 00 for the type-defined order, 2C 00 00 for IEEE 754), so the rewrite changes no offsets or lengths.

The rewrite is checked:

  • the list must be the footer's last field, with one entry per leaf column, each one of the two known encodings, or the output is rejected and deleted;
  • after the rewrite the footer is read back, and its column orders must equal the inputs'.

Inputs written without column orders (by writers older than parquet-format 2.4) get the type-defined order, which is how readers interpret such files.

The tests check every column chunk's statistics in the output against its source's, as pyarrow reads them, with NaN, -0.0, +0.0 and infinities in the float columns.

items.title: The output file
items.text:
part where it comes from row groups every input's, in input order, unchanged column chunks copied as bytes: the same pages, dictionary page, encodings and compression column chunk statistics the inputs' (min, max, null count, distinct count) page indexes the inputs' column and offset indexes, where they have them bloom filters the inputs', where they have them Parquet schema the first input's key-value metadata the first input's, including ARROW:schema column orders the inputs' (Column orders) created_by parquet-rs, which writes the footer

Row groups are not merged or split: an output written from files of one small row group each has as many small row groups. Read it with a reader that handles many row groups, or rewrite it once if a few large row groups are needed.

items.title: Requirements on the inputs
items.text:
Every input must have the first input's:

  • Parquet schema (field names, types, repetition and logical types);
  • key-value metadata (so ARROW:schema describes every row group);
  • column orders (so every row group's statistics follow the same order).

items.title: Cases concat refuses
items.text:
concat returns an error and writes nothing when:

case Python Rust no inputs ValueError Error::NoInputs the output path is an input path ValueError Error::OutputIsInput an input differs in schema, metadata or column orders ValueError Error::Incompatible an input is not a Parquet file ValueError Error::Parquet an input cannot be opened OSError Error::Io

If the copy fails after the output file has been created, the output file is deleted.

items.title: Python
items.text:
pq-glue needs Python 3.10 or later. It has no Python dependencies.

pip install pq-glue

or with uv:

uv add pq-glue

Wheels are built for Linux (x86_64, aarch64, armv7), macOS (x86_64, arm64) and Windows (x64). Each wheel uses the stable ABI (abi3), so one wheel covers every Python version from 3.10.

items.title: Rust
items.text:
cargo add pq-glue

The crate depends only on the parquet crate, with no compression codecs: it never decompresses a page.

items.title: Quickstart
items.text:
Write two files with the same schema:

import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

schema = pa.schema([("id", pa.string()), ("tags", pa.list_(pa.string()))])
pq.write_table(pa.table({"id": ["Q1", "Q2"], "tags": [["a"], []]}, schema=schema), "a.parquet")
pq.write_table(pa.table({"id": ["Q3"], "tags": [None]}, schema=schema), "b.parquet")

Concatenate them. concat returns the number of rows written:

>>> import pq_glue
>>> pq_glue.concat(["a.parquet", "b.parquet"], "ab.parquet")
3

The output has both files' rows, in order, and one row group per input row group:

>>> pq.read_table("ab.parquet").to_pylist()
[{'id': 'Q1', 'tags': ['a']}, {'id': 'Q2', 'tags': []}, {'id': 'Q3', 'tags': None}]
>>> pq.ParquetFile("ab.parquet").metadata.num_row_groups
2

Files with different schemas are refused, and no output is written:

>>> other = pa.table({"id": ["Q4"]})
>>> pq.write_table(other, "c.parquet")
>>> pq_glue.concat(["a.parquet", "c.parquet"], "ac.parquet")
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
ValueError: c.parquet has other schema than a.parquet
>>> import os
>>> os.path.exists("ac.parquet")
False

items.title: Building and testing
items.text:
The tools: a Rust toolchain, uv, just, and for the lints taplo, whitespace-format and cargo-machete.

just py         # maturin develop, then pytest
just test-ci    # cargo test and the doc tests
just clippy     # clippy on every target and feature, warnings as errors
just t          # ty, the type checker
just pc         # formatting and lints (as pre-commit runs them)

items.title: Commits
items.text: Commit messages follow Conventional Commits (feat:, fix:, docs:, ci: ...); the conventional-pre-commit hook checks them. release-plz.toml groups the changelog by these prefixes.

items.title: Documentation
items.text:
The site is built with Zensical from docs/site/ and zensical.toml. The Python API reference is generated by mkdocstrings from the package's docstrings and the compiled module's stub (python/pq_glue/_pq_glue.pyi).

just docs-serve   # build, serve and rebuild on change
just docs-check   # strict build, site checks, and the pages' examples as tests

docs/scripts/check_site.py checks that every page is in the nav, that internal links and anchors resolve, that every page has a description matching its llms.txt entry, and that every public name is in the API reference. docs/conftest.py runs each page's Python examples with pytest (pytest docs); a pycon block's output must match.

items.title: Publishing
items.text: .github/workflows/site.yml builds the site on every push to master and publishes it to the gh-pages branch, served at https://lmmx.github.io/pq-glue/. A pull request from this repository gets a preview under pr-preview/pr-<number>/, linked from a comment on the pull request and removed when it closes. Previews start once the repository's Pages source is set to the gh-pages branch.

items.title: PyPI
items.text:
Run the Deploy Release workflow (or just release locally). It:

  1. bumps the version in pyproject.toml with uv version --bump patch (or minor, major);
  2. sets the crate's version in Cargo.toml to match;
  3. commits chore(release): bump 🐍 -> vX.Y.Z and tags py-X.Y.Z;
  4. pushes the commit and the tag.

The tag starts the CI workflow, which builds the wheels and the sdist and uploads them to PyPI with Trusted Publishing (the pypi environment). The repository needs a PyPI trusted publisher for lmmx/pq-glue, workflow CI.yml, environment pypi.

items.title: crates.io
items.text: just ship-rust runs release-plz: it updates the version and changelog, commits chore(release): 🦀 Upgrades, pushes, and publishes the crate with a pq-glue-vX.Y.Z tag.

items.title: pq-glue (Rust)
items.text:
The crate's API documentation is on docs.rs.

item what it is pq_glue::concat(inputs: &[PathBuf], output: &Path) -> Result<u64> concatenate the inputs into output, returning the rows written pq_glue::Error the errors concat returns: NoInputs, OutputIsInput, Incompatible, Io, Parquet, Footer pq_glue::footer::restore_column_orders rewrite a file's footer column orders in place 
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

fn main() -> pq_glue::Result<()> {
    let inputs = [PathBuf::from("a.parquet"), PathBuf::from("b.parquet")];
    let rows = pq_glue::concat(&inputs, Path::new("ab.parquet"))?;
    println!("{rows} rows");
    Ok(())
}

The python feature builds the Python extension module; it is only for maturin.

items.title: pq_glue
items.text: Concatenate Parquet files by copying their encoded row groups, without decoding them.

items.title: __version__ module-attribute
items.text: __version__: str

items.title: concat
items.text:
concat(sources: Sequence[str | PathLike[str]], dst: str | PathLike[str]) -> int

Concatenate Parquet files that share one schema into one file.

Each input's row groups are copied to dst as they are encoded (pages, dictionaries, statistics), in input order, without being decoded. The output has the first input's schema and key-value metadata, and the inputs' column orders, page indexes and bloom filters.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default sources Sequence[str | PathLike[str]]

The Parquet files to concatenate, in order. Each must have the first one's Parquet schema, key-value metadata and column orders.

required dst str | PathLike[str]

The file to write, created or truncated. It is removed if the copy fails part way, and must not be one of sources.

required

Returns:

Type Description int

The number of rows written.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If there are no sources, dst is one of them, a source is not a Parquet file, or the sources differ in schema, key-value metadata or column orders.

OSError

If a source cannot be opened or dst cannot be written.
